title: tapBoth runs exactly one of its two handlers and does not replace the Result it observes
notes: The deliberate pair of 01-result-lifting/result-tap-and-tap-error-observe-without-changing, which pins the one-sided observers. `tap` fires only on success and `tapError` only on failure, so neither case can see an observer that runs on BOTH variants; `tapBoth` is the member where running exactly one handler is the whole contract, and the order of the first two lines is what says so — one `tapBoth` call pushed `ok …` and the other pushed `error …`, so neither call ran both handlers and neither ran the wrong one. The last two lines prove the observed Result was passed through unchanged, exactly as the tap/tapError case proves it: `Ada Lovelace` survives to `unwrapOr` on the success path and `none` on the failure path, so the observation replaced neither variant. Like `flatten`, `tapBoth` was implemented and tested on the runtime (poc/src/runtime/result.ts) while no `.sm` program could call it, and the refusal was SMITHERS1301 — an unrecognized member leaves the Result unconsumed — rather than an unknown-property error, so nothing went red while the member sat unreachable.

xfail.reason: MEASURED 2026-08-28 through `run.mjs --backend both --filter result-tap-both`, not assumed: the fork REFUSES this program with [SMITHERS1301@14:19, SMITHERS1301@17:18] — 'Result value is not consumed' — while the reference accepts it and prints all four lines. Same cause as 01-result-lifting/result-flatten-collapses-one-level-of-nesting and it retires with it: `compiler/forkbridge/lowering.go.txt` holds the fork's own `resultConsumerMembers` list plus its `SmithersOk`/`SmithersErr` prelude classes, and none of the three knows `tapBoth`. Fail-CLOSED: the fork rejects a valid program rather than running an invalid one, so this is a reachability gap and not a soundness hole. Note for whoever closes it that `tapBoth` needs the handler-object validation the runtime already performs — a missing branch panics rather than being silently skipped, the same way `match` validates — so a fork implementation that only adds the name to the list would satisfy this case while diverging on a malformed handler object that no case yet probes.
xfail.doc: specification/failures.mdx, "Matching and Transformation", lists the required observation members as `tap tapAsync tapError tapErrorAsync tapBoth tapBothAsync` under the heading "Observation, which MUST NOT change the Result". Both halves of that sentence are pinned here: `tapBoth` exists, and it does not change the Result.
